Native R functional trajectories: Phase 2 scientific core

native-api.Rd

Explicit, Python-independent functions for common-grid trajectories, preprocessing, quadrature-weighted dense FPCA, sampled planar kinematics, trajectory distances, basic recurrence analysis, and base graphics.

Usage

etr_trajectory_set(time, values, curve_ids = NULL, dimension_names = NULL,
    metadata = NULL, coordinate_system = "unknown", time_unit = "unknown",
    provenance = list(), python_boundary_mode = FALSE)

etr_trajectory_source_class_record(x)

etr_validate(x, require_complete = FALSE)

etr_from_long(data, curve_columns, time_column = "time", value_columns = c("x", "y"),
    metadata_columns = NULL, coordinate_system = "unknown", time_unit = "unknown",
    provenance = NULL)

etr_as_long(x)

etr_subset(x, curves, python_boundary_mode = FALSE)

etr_dimension(x, dimension)

etr_summary(x)

etr_resample(x, new_time, max_gap = Inf)

etr_interpolate_gaps(x, max_gap)

etr_normalize_time(x, method = c("unit", "origin"))

etr_center(x, method = c("first", "mean"))

etr_smooth(x, window = 5L)

etr_scale_channels(x, scaling = c("none", "dimension_sd"))

etr_velocity(x)

etr_acceleration(x)

etr_speed(x)

etr_heading(x)

etr_path_length(x)

etr_cumulative_path_length(x)

etr_tortuosity(x)

etr_l2_distance(a, b, time, dimension_weights = NULL,
  python_boundary_mode = FALSE)

etr_pairwise_l2(x, dimension_weights = NULL, python_boundary_mode = FALSE)

etr_frechet(a, b, dimension_weights = NULL, return_coupling = FALSE,
  python_boundary_mode = FALSE)

etr_dtw(a, b, dimension_weights = NULL, window_radius = NULL,
  step_pattern = "symmetric1", normalize = FALSE, return_path = FALSE,
  python_boundary_mode = FALSE)

etr_pairwise_dtw(x, dimension_weights = NULL, dimensions = NULL,
  window_radius = NULL, step_pattern = "symmetric1", normalize = FALSE,
  python_boundary_mode = FALSE)

etr_trapezoid_weights(time, normalize = FALSE,
  python_boundary_mode = FALSE)

etr_fit_fpca(x, n_components = 0.95, scaling = c("none", "dimension_sd"))

etr_fit_mfpca(x, n_components = 0.95, scaling = c("none", "dimension_sd"))

etr_fpca_scores(fit)

etr_fpca_variance_frame(fit)

etr_transform_fpca(fit, x)

etr_reconstruct_fpca(fit, n_components = NULL, scores = NULL)

etr_recurrence_matrix(x, curve = 1L, radius = NULL, theiler = 0L,
  metric = "euclidean", target_recurrence_rate = NULL,
  dimensions = NULL, theiler_window_units = "samples",
  sparse_output = FALSE)

etr_cross_recurrence_matrix(a, b, radius = NULL, metric = "euclidean",
  target_recurrence_rate = NULL, curve_a = NULL, curve_b = NULL,
  dimensions_a = NULL, dimensions_b = NULL,
  sparse_output = FALSE)

etr_rqa_metrics(recurrence, min_diagonal_length = 2L, min_vertical_length = 2L)

etr_plot_trajectories(x, max_curves = 40L, invert_y = TRUE, ...)

etr_plot_fpca_variance(fit, cumulative = TRUE, ...)

etr_plot_recurrence(recurrence, ...)

Arguments

time

Strictly increasing finite time vector; in distance methods, matched observation times. The explicit Python boundary mode of etr_trapezoid_weights() additionally casts a complex atomic time vector to its real part, matching NumPy's complex ndarray dtype=float conversion, and accepts ASCII decimal strings with underscores between digits.

values

Numeric 3D array ordered curve, time, dimension. NA is allowed in stored objects.

curve_ids

Unique identifiers for curves.

dimension_names

Unique measurement channel names.

metadata

Optional curve-level data frame.

coordinate_system

Explicit coordinate semantics, e.g. pixels.

time_unit

Explicit temporal units, e.g. ms or s.

provenance

Optional JSON-like named native R list of source and preprocessing decisions. For etr_from_long, the source audit is added by default and user-supplied named keys are applied as shallow overrides.

x

Native trajectory set, or a fitted object as documented in the specific function.

sparse_output

Opt-in native sparse recurrence construction for one-dimensional finite fixed-radius states. FALSE (default) preserves the original dense R API; TRUE returns Matrix sparse adjacency with inclusive-radius pairs and, for auto recurrence, the declared Theiler exclusion. Multidimensional and target-rate sparse construction remain unsupported, and Matrix/S3 output differs from Python scipy CSR/dataclass identity.

require_complete

Whether to reject missing samples.

data

Long-format data frame with individual gaze samples.

curve_columns

Names of curve identifier columns.

time_column

Name of time variable.

value_columns

Names of measurement variables.

metadata_columns

Optional curve-constant metadata columns.

curves

Unique 1-based integer curve indices or string identifiers by default; opt-in source boundary mode uses 0-based/negative integer indices, including empty selections.

dimension

Channel index or channel name.

new_time

Target time grid (no extrapolation).

max_gap

Maximum allowed observed time interval for explicit interpolation.

method

Declared normalization or centering rule.

window

Odd integer running-mean window size.

scaling

Channel scaling policy: none or dimension_sd.

a

Numeric point-by-channel matrix.

b

Numeric point-by-channel matrix with matching channels.

dimension_weights

Finite, non-negative channel weights.

return_coupling

If TRUE, return the 0-based deterministic discrete Fréchet coupling and local costs.

window_radius

Optional non-negative integer Sakoe-Chiba index-window radius for DTW.

step_pattern

DTW transition weighting: symmetric1 or symmetric2.

return_path

If TRUE, return 0-based DTW path, local and weighted costs, and provenance.

normalize

For DTW, TRUE normalizes only the symmetric2 step pattern by n_points_a + n_points_b. For trapezoidal weights, a scalar with Python 1.2 truthiness semantics: FALSE, zero, empty string and zero complex keep original weights. Nonzero numeric scalars, nonempty strings and, in the explicit Python boundary mode, nonzero, infinite or NaN-valued complex scalars normalize to unit total. Empty/nonempty lists have container truthiness in source-boundary mode. Dimensioned atomic flags in that mode use the truthiness of their sole element and reject other sizes. General Python object truthiness remains outside the qualified domain.

python_boundary_mode

For pairwise L2 and DTW, TRUE also propagates bounded frozen Python 1.2 numeric coercion and nonfinite L2 semantics; otherwise existing native defaults remain. For Fréchet and DTW, TRUE also enables rectangular nested 2D point sequences, numeric-string/Boolean/complex matrices and weighted NumPy float-domain conversions. Defaults remain strict scientific numeric matrices. Logical flag requesting a bounded native Python 1.2 source-input compatibility domain. For trapezoidal weighting it includes stated exceptional grids, complex ndarray-style time casting, and Python scalar/container truthiness. For functional L2 distance it permits numeric-string/Boolean/complex matrices and dimension weights with explicit NumPy-style real conversion. The L2 source mode also allows infinity and NaN-valued weights where Python propagates the same nonfinite arithmetic; input NaN trajectory coordinates remain rejected. FALSE uses native R finite validation. Neither value invokes Python, and full source-domain parity is not claimed.

For trajectory construction and subsetting, TRUE enables NaN observations, empty curve and channel axes, rectangular nested mixed numeric-like values, mixed scalar label lists, and ID-indexed metadata. Complex arrays cast to real with a warning. Subset indices use zero-based and negative indexing after coercion. FALSE uses strict native R defaults.

metric

Distance metric for recurrence and cross-recurrence: euclidean (L2), cityblock (L1), or chebyshev (L-infinity). The default is Euclidean.

n_components

Integer component count or, for fitting, a variance fraction strictly between 0 and 1.

fit

Native etr_fpca fit.

scores

Optional finite numeric FPCA score vector (one external curve) or numeric matrix (curves by fitted components). When supplied, reconstructs these external scores to an unlabelled curve-by-time-by-dimension numeric array. When omitted, fitted curves are returned as the original native trajectory collection.

curve

Curve ID or 1-based index.

radius

Optional fixed finite non-negative recurrence radius. Specify exactly one of radius or target_recurrence_rate.

target_recurrence_rate

Optional probability strictly between zero and one, selecting the source-aligned target-density threshold policy. Distance ties may prevent an exact target rate.

dimensions

Optional ordered selected channel names for native recurrence sources and pairwise DTW; NULL retains all channels. For pairwise DTW, the order controls dimension-weight alignment.

theiler_window_units

Theiler interval units: samples or compatible physical time on a sufficiently regular observed grid.

curve_a,curve_b

Required curve identifiers for trajectory-set cross-recurrence inputs; NULL for numeric matrices.

dimensions_a,dimensions_b

Required matching ordered state-channel names for trajectory-set cross-recurrence; NULL for numeric matrices or already embedded state spaces.

theiler

Excluded sample lag for auto-recurrence.

recurrence

Native etr_recurrence object. For etr_rqa_metrics(), native sparse Matrix auto- and cross- recurrence are supported without dense allocation. Sparse auto-RQA uses upper-triangle diagonals and full-matrix vertical runs; sparse cross-RQA uses every diagonal and full-matrix vertical runs. Both include finite-border runs. Source-style line statistics require approximately regular time grids, and cross-RQA requires matching step sizes on the two declared axes. Undefined sparse statistics use NaN; dense defaults remain unchanged.

min_diagonal_length

Minimum counted diagonal line length.

min_vertical_length

Minimum counted vertical run length.

max_curves

Maximum plotted curves.

invert_y

Whether to invert the planar screen Y axis.

cumulative

Plot cumulative explained variance.

...

Additional base R plotting arguments.

Details

Phase 2 currently implements dense-grid methods, not sparse or asynchronous PACE. FPCA returns the same weighted-PCA mathematical target as the Python backend but makes no guarantee that eigenvector signs are identical. The recurrence methods use dense matrices and explicit fixed radii and are not full RQA parity. Input preparation is explicit, without hidden interpolation, missingness repair, smoothing, or coordinate normalization.

Frozen Python TrajectorySet source-scientific class record

After explicitly constructing a native etr_trajectory_set(..., python_boundary_mode=TRUE), the function etr_trajectory_source_class_record(x) returns an inspectable typed native R scientific class record with the eight frozen Python 1.2 source dataclass scientific fields in their original order, metadata indexed by curve ID, and the three shape properties n_curves, n_time, n_dimensions. It identifies the native method surface: etr_dimension for named channel retrieval, etr_subset(x, indices, python_boundary_mode=TRUE) for source zero-based signed indices, and etr_with_values for value replacement with shallow provenance updates.

This is deliberately NOT a real frozen Python TrajectorySet dataclass, pandas container, complete NumPy coercion implementation, or independent scientific certification. The source-qualified native R data-and-method domain excludes Python-specific object reflection, arbitrary pandas indexes, heterogeneous label collisions, and Python exception/warning class identity. See docs/native-trajectory-source-class-record-20261112.md.

Value

Depends on the function: a native trajectory collection, native FPCA result, numeric matrix/vector, recurrence result, data frame, or base-R plot.

See also

et_fit_mfpca, et_call

Examples

t <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 9)
v <- array(0, c(6L, length(t), 2L))
for (i in seq_len(6L)) {
  v[i, , 1L] <- sin(2*pi*t + i/6)
  v[i, , 2L] <- cos(2*pi*t + i/6)
}
x <- etr_trajectory_set(t, v, paste0("c", 1:6), c("x", "y"))
fit <- etr_fit_mfpca(x, n_components = 1L)
stopifnot(nrow(etr_fpca_scores(fit)) == 6L)
